To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
noctuid moths have ears that are highly sensitive to ultrasound and that the sensitivity of these ears is dynamic, changing with the sound intensity.

(1) The ear of a noctuid moth mechanically tunes up in a hysteretic manner to high frequencies in response to low frequency sounds, (2) the ear's mechanical sensitivity is dependent on the intensity of the sound and (3) the tuning of the ear to high frequencies persists for a period after the stimulus ends.
the moth's ear is a nonlinear dynamic system that mechanically tunes up in response to the sound intensity of an incident sound and keeps the ear tuned up in anticipation of a bat's possible return.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensory biology and ecology of insects that are preyed upon by echolocative bats.
the evolution of hearing in noctuid moths.
the sensory systems of insects, and in particular with the hearing systems of noctuid moths and their acoustic predators, the bats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the moth ear is a sophisticated and highly tuned system that is capable of adapting to the echolocation calls of its bat predator.

moth ears are more sophisticated than previously thought.
